boundary: This file records what the pinned commaai/opendbc Toyota implementation does. It is prior art for semantic roles and integration architecture, not evidence that a TSS3 vehicle reuses any CAN identifier, wire layout, producer ECU, timing, or safety limit. Target firmware and captures remain authoritative.

tss2.architectural_fact: The camera is treated as the longitudinal-control source on TSS2 cars unless the RADAR_ACC flag selects a radar-originated ACC architecture.

secoc_tss2.architectural_fact: SecOC is layered onto the TSS2 platform model rather than replacing the state, ownership, actuation-limit, or stock-suppression model.

lateral_torque_command.controller_behavior: Generated every CarController update. On SecOC platforms the message is MACed with its own message counter.

lateral_angle_command.controller_behavior: Generated on frame modulo 2 for TSS2. When angle control is selected, the torque command is zeroed and LTA angle control becomes active; SecOC platforms also emit the authenticated companion.

longitudinal_command.controller_behavior: Openpilot longitudinal runs on frame modulo 3. On the SecOC profile ACC_CONTROL carries zero acceleration while ACC_CONTROL_2 carries the signed acceleration command and its own SecOC counter.
longitudinal_command.ownership: TSS2 camera unless RADAR_ACC; radar-originated ACC can be disabled via diagnostic communication control before openpilot assumes longitudinal ownership.

cruise_state_and_cancel.behavior: CarState selects different availability/fault sources for unsupported-DSU and TSS2 architectures. Stock-long cancel uses PCM_CRUISE on unsupported-DSU cars and ACC_CONTROL otherwise.

driver_ui.controller_behavior: Sent on frame modulo 20 or immediately on alert/cancel transitions; selected stock camera fields are preserved when available.

actuation_and_safety_contract.note: These are implementation limits in the pinned older-Toyota port, not values to transplant into an uncharacterized TSS3 EPS.
actuation_and_safety_contract.secoc_lta2_actuation_policy: The pinned Toyota Panda safety hook allows the 0x131 frame shape but rejects any STEERING_LTA_2 actuation request or nonzero angle; pinned SecOC control is therefore torque-only at the safety boundary.

stock_source_ownership.camera_longitudinal: TSS2 non-RADAR_ACC uses camera-side ACC state and is designed around replacing camera-originated command traffic.
stock_source_ownership.radar_longitudinal: RADAR_ACC requires a different ownership path; openpilot can disable radar transmission with UDS CommunicationControl to 0x750/subaddress 0xF when experimental longitudinal is selected.
stock_source_ownership.generic_replacement_rule: Toyota safety marks replaced command/UI frames with check_relay so generic Panda forwarding blocks the stock copy when openpilot transmits the replacement.
stock_source_ownership.implication: Finding the TSS3 command payload is insufficient: the physical/logical producer, route, duplicate-suppression point, and safe stock fallback must also be recovered.

secoc_layer.architectural_fact: The controller keeps independent LKA, LTA, and ACC SecOC message counters and resets all three when RESET_CNT changes.

platform_identity.eps_role: The upstream source explicitly says EPS firmware describes lateral API changes, including use of LTA for lane keeping and rejection of LKA messages.
platform_identity.porting_implication: Collect and bind camera, radar, and EPS firmware identities before choosing a TSS3 DBC/control profile; EPS software identity is evidence about lateral API generation, not merely a fingerprint string.

radar_generation.implication: Even observation inputs moved with Toyota generation changes; TSS3 radar/camera state should be re-censused rather than inherited from TSS-P/TSS2.
